text:
IncidentBot: P1 - inference-serving latency spike detected in prod (region: eu-west1). Paging oncall @Ava (oncall). Automated alert: 90th pct token latency > 2.5s for 6m.

Ava (oncall): ack - I'm on it, joining thread. 

Marta (support): seeing customer reports — a few enterprise customers with 502/503s and slow streaming. Only started ~05:22 UTC. Putting affected customers into a ticket.

Ava (oncall): quick summary from dashboards: runtime CPU high on several pods, gRPC queue depth climbing, some OOM kills on runtime-2/3. Not sure if infra autoscaler failed or model fallback routing misfired.

Rahul (secondary): oncoming in ~15m. If we need escalation to infra or security before then, call me now.

Lin (runtime): digging into the runtime logs now. Running `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=redwood-runtime -o wide` then `kubectl logs runtime-2 -n prod --tail=200`. I see repeated `KVCache miss` + `slow_attention` traces, and some pods show `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError` (native JNI alloc). Suspect a bad batch/sequence length spike.

Diego (infra-oncall): checking autoscaler and node pool. I see the cluster autoscaler didn't scale because of quota on GPUs in eu-west1. Opening a ticket to cloud quota. Meanwhile, I can spin up fallback CPU-backed nodes to relieve non-GPU workloads. ETA ~7m.

Ava (oncall): good. Lin, can runtime trigger model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) for affected routes? We want to reduce memory/KV pressure.

Lin (runtime): yes, we have a rollout key `runtime.fallback.variant.small-v2`. I can toggle it for route `generation/default` to force small-v2. Command (admin-only):
```
POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/config/rollouts
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "route": "generation/default",
  "feature": "runtime.fallback.variant",
  "value": "small-v2",
  "scope": "eu-west1",
  "actor": "Ava (oncall)"
}
```
I'll prepare the change but hold until infra confirms temporary capacity.

Marta (support): FYI customers impacted: AcmeCorp (errors since 05:24 UTC), BloomHealth (intermittent). I'll place them on incident notification list and send mitigations note once we have concrete steps.

SecurityBot: Notified security on-call. Initial traffic patterns show increased request fanout from a small set of IPs in RU range. Marking for investigation.

Diego (infra-oncall): spun up two `n1-standard-8` CPU nodes in the emergency pool and cordoned a couple of high-memory nodes for investigation. Node addition confirmed: `nodepool-emergency-1 +2 nodes` -> Ready.

Ava (oncall): Lin, flip fallback to small-v2 in eu-west1 now to reduce memory pressure. I'll monitor.

Lin (runtime): Done. Patch applied. Routing table shows ~42% traffic switched to small-v2 for `generation/default` in eu-west1.

Ava (oncall): immediate metrics: 90th pct latency dropped from 2.6s -> 1.1s, error rate from 6% -> 1.2%. Streaming latency still slightly high but improving.

Marta (support): telling customers we've applied a temporary routing fallback to a smaller model to stabilize latency. Requested permission to keep customers updated every 15m.

Rahul (secondary): joining thread now. Quick question: who owns KV cache warmup? runtime team? If we see a prefix miss storm we might need proactive priming.

Lin (runtime): runtime owns KV cache. For this incident: after fallback's stable, we should run `cache-priming` across commonly requested prefixes. Command: `./tools/cache-prime --route generation/default --prefetch-file top-prefixes.txt --concurrency 10`. I'll schedule this in 10m.

Diego (infra-oncall): infra note: autoscaler quotas are still being processed; GCP quota request pending approval — ETA unknown. Recommend adding a longer-term mitigation: allow CPU fallback node pool to autoscale for time windows. Filed infra ticket INF-482.

SecurityBot: initial investigation: the RU IPs appear to be legitimate customers behind a corporate NAT (ASN 12345). No evidence of payload tampering or repeated malformed requests. We'll keep monitoring.

Ava (oncall): handoff plan: I'm handing primary to Rahul in 12m. Open action items:
- Lin: run cache-priming and monitor KV miss rate (Ongoing)
- Diego: monitor emergency node pool and try to resolve quota (INF-482)
- Marta: keep customers notified, update incident ticket with mitigation note
- SecurityBot: continue traffic monitoring for anomalies

Rahul (secondary): I'll be primary in 12m. If anything degrades post-handoff I'll page infra and runtime. Also will keep the fallback routing on until we see stable 90th pct < 1.2s for 30m.

Ava (oncall): note for handoff doc: runbook link - https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ONCALL/pages/Inference+Latency+Spike. Key runbook sections: "fallback routing", "cache-priming", "emergency node pool".

Lin (runtime): cache-priming started, concurrency 8, prefetched ~1.2k prefixes. KV miss rate down 78% in the last 4m. Pushing logs to `/var/log/runtime/kv_priming.log`.

Diego (infra-oncall): emergency node pool stable. Watching pod restart counts; 2 pods still restarted earlier but now healthy.

Marta (support): customers acknowledged mitigation, AcmeCorp back to normal for now. Leaving incident notification open until Rahul confirms stabilization after handoff.

Ava (oncall): handing primary -> Rahul now. Rahul, I'm leaving a short handoff note in the oncall doc: `Handoff at 05:39 UTC. Fallback small-v2 enabled for eu-west1. Cache priming running. Infra emergency nodes up. Quota request INF-482 pending.`

Rahul (secondary): took over as primary. Thanks @Ava. I'm monitoring. Next check in 15m, will evaluate rollback of fallback if stable.

IncidentBot: Incident P1 still active - mitigation applied (routing fallback). Logs and actions recorded.

SecurityBot: will follow up if traffic pattern changes or if we see unusual auth failures.

Rahul (primary): 15m check: 90th pct latency 1.05s, error rate 0.9%, KV miss rate steady low. I'm going to schedule a post-incident follow-up epics: retrofit better node pool fallback policy and automations for quota shortage.

Ava (oncall): leaving final note: postmortem owner? I can take initial draft but want infra + runtime co-authors. Assigning to Ava + Lin + Diego.

Marta (support): I'll add customer impact details to the incident ticket and send internal comms.

Rahul (primary): closing handoff thread — I'll keep monitoring until we stop the routing fallback per runbook. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: Incident P1 moved to 'Mitigated'. Remaining tasks tracked in INF-482 and the incident ticket.
